candidate.answerReason: The displayed dimensions give region areas 21, 20, 15, 6, and 4 square feet. Assigning increasing flower prices to decreasing areas minimizes the cost, yielding $108 and matching A.

methods.label: Assign cheaper flowers to larger regions
methods.explanation:
The number of flowers in each region equals its area in square feet. We first find these areas, then compare possible price assignments.

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_10B_Q04_question_fig1.svg)

The upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right regions have areas
\[
4\cdot5=20,\quad 7\cdot3=21,\quad
6\cdot1=6,\quad 5\cdot3=15.
\]
The middle region has width \(6-4=2\) feet and height \(5-3=2\) feet, so its area is \(4\) square feet. The five areas in decreasing order are therefore \(21,20,15,6,4\).

There are five regions and five flower types, so each price is used once. To see which assignment is cheapest, suppose a larger region of area \(a\) receives flowers priced at \(p\), while a smaller region of area \(b\) receives flowers priced at \(q\), where \(a>b\) and \(p>q\). Swapping the flower types saves
\[
(ap+bq)-(aq+bp)=(a-b)(p-q)>0.
\]
Thus putting the cheaper flowers in the larger region reduces the cost. Starting with any assignment, put the cheapest remaining type in the largest remaining region, swapping if necessary. Each required swap lowers the cost, so this process proves that increasing prices should be matched with decreasing areas.

Assign asters, begonias, cannas, dahlias, and Easter lilies to areas \(21,20,15,6,4\), respectively. The least cost, in dollars, is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&21(1)+20(1.50)+15(2)+6(2.50)+4(3)\\
&\qquad=21+30+30+15+12=108.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{108}\) dollars, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
